problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 & -3 \\ 3 & -3 & 7 & -2 \\ 5 & -2 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

activity_context.topic_title: Finding Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

examples.knowledge_point: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Column Operations
examples.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & -2 & -2 & 4 \\ -4 & -4 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Find a $3\times 3$ determinant that has the same value.

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of $a_{23}$ equal to zero.*
examples.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of $a_{23}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (or column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & -2 & -2 & 4 \\ -4 & -4 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-2){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -10 & 3 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -10 & 3 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 8 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 \\ -1 & -10 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 8 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 \\ -1 & -10 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 3 & 5 & 8 & 6 \\ 4 & 3 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{23}$ equal to zero.*
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{23}=-2$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 3 & 5 & 8 & 6 \\ 4 & 3 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 0 & 13 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 11 & 9 & 0 & 26 \\ 6 & 4 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 0 & 13 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & 5 \\ 11 & 9 & 0 & 26 \\ 6 & 4 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 13 \\ 11 & 9 & 26 \\ 6 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 13 \\ 11 & 9 & 26 \\ 6 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
